text:
sara: FYI — incoming escalation from AcmeApps. After the v4.2.1 model rollout some customers see tool-call failures. Posting logs from the customer below.
jamie: ah — is this the canary roll we pushed last night?
mike: yes that was v4.2.1, canary -> gradual. Any error message from their side?
sara: they get a schema validation error from our function router: `tool_call_rejected: invalid_args: missing required field 'order_id'` even though the prompt includes order_id.
sara: example payload they sent: 
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-llm-4.2.1",
  "input": " refund order 12345 ",
  "tools": ["orders.lookup", "payments.refund"]
}
```
jamie: weird. Could be a tool selection mismatch — maybe model is returning `tool: payments.refund` but a different schema expected?
devon: @jamie can you check the tool schema mapping we ship with 4.2.1? We made a small change to optional fields last patch.
ops-bot: deploy-log: canary rollout v4.2.1 -> 10% traffic started 2026-02-14T03:12:10Z
mike: repro notes from CS: they pasted the `tool_call` object returned by the model: 
```json
{
  "tool": "payments.refund",
  "args": { "amount": "100.00", "currency": "USD" }
}
```
sara: their orders.refund function expects `{order_id: string, reason?: string}` so args don't match, router rejects. But the user prompt asked for refund by order id.
jamie: so two possibilities: (1) model chooses wrong tool (payments.refund) instead of orders.refund, or (2) arguments are being mutated/stripped during postprocessing.
devon: I ran a quick diff of the tool-choice logits across model versions — 4.2.1 shows higher p(payments.refund) for short prompts vs v4.1.7. Could be slight distributional shift.
mike: can we repro locally with a minimal prompt? I'll run a small loop hitting the canary model with sample prompts.
sara: CS asked for rollback if more customers are affected. We should triage impact first.
mike: quick results: 30 calls with `refund order 12345` -> v4.1.7 chose orders.refund 93% of the time; v4.2.1 chose payments.refund 68% of the time.
jamie: that's a clear behavioral regression in tool selection. Not a schema bug in router.
devon: agree. Also noticed 4.2.1 strips numeric `order_` tokens in some completions due to new tokenization normalizer we enabled. That could explain missing `order_id` in some cases.
sara: customer impacted: AcmeApps, 6 failing requests in last hour, blocked checkout flows. Escalation severity: P1 from CS.
mike: propose immediate action: pause canary + rollback model routing for production customers who opted into canary; open emergency rollback for global rollout.
jamie: +1. Also add a temporary rule in router: if model returns `payments.refund` but prompt contains pattern `order\s*\d+`, prefer `orders.refund` routing.
devon: I can push that heuristic as a short-term mitigation while we revert the token normalizer. I'll open a PR.
sara: I'll inform AcmeApps support contact and offer immediate routing to v4.1.7 for their project.
ops-bot: incident-created: INC-2026-0427 by sara (P1) — assigned to eng-ml, eng-runtime.
mike: follow-ups: (a) rollback canary, (b) disable token normalizer in build, (c) add regression test for tool choice on refund prompts, (d) postmortem if rollout caused outage.
jamie: logging item: capture model logits + raw tokens for canary requests for 24h to diagnose.
sara: I'll update the ticket and ping customer after rollback. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
